lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, look at the door. Deedee measured me two times since you left.
lines.script: [proud] Tata, look at the door. [matter-of-fact] Deedee measured me TWO times since you left.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I got one too. Mine's the low one.
lines.script: [proud, eager] I got one too. [matter-of-fact] Mine's the LOW one.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Twenty years ago I'd have caught that thing before it got to the fence.
lines.script: [boastful] Twenty years ago I'd have caught that thing... [wistful] before it got to the fence.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Tom. You stay in front of those girls.
lines.script: [serious, quiet] Tom. [firm] You stay in FRONT of those girls.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: A WHAT climbed in my window?
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, shocked] A WHAT climbed in my window?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It has EYES! The mud has EYES!
lines.script: [scared, shrill] It has EYES! [shrill, urgent] The mud has EYES!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Forty years in this kitchen. I've had ants. I've had a raccoon. I have never had THAT.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, outraged] Forty years in this kitchen. [warm Long Island accent, brisk] I've had ants. I've had a raccoon. [warm Long Island accent, slowly, appalled] I have never had... THAT.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's so brown. It's the brownest thing I've ever seen.
lines.script: [disgusted] It's so brown. [dramatic, slowly] It's the BROWNEST thing I've ever seen.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's running for the pond!
lines.script: [alarmed, rushed] It's running for the pond!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It talks.
lines.script: [flat, stunned] It talks.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: It talks AND it steals.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, dry, exasperated] It talks AND it steals.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: I've been bitten ten thousand times in my life. Not one of them ever said a word first.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, offended] I've been bitten ten thousand times in my life. [warm Long Island accent, deadpan] Not ONE of them ever said a word first.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then nobody goes near the water. Stay close.
lines.script: [firm, quiet] Then nobody goes near the water. [gentle] Stay close.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: A MARBLE! There's a marble with a bug in it!
lines.script: [delighted, shouts] A MARBLE! [amazed] There's a marble with a bug in it!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That's a dragonfly. It's inside an orange rock. Its wings are open and it's not moving.
lines.script: [careful] That's a dragonfly. It's inside an orange rock. [hushed, curious] Its wings are open... and it's not moving.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Look at the grass. It's grey. Just this bit, the size of my hand.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, puzzled] Look at the grass. [warm Long Island accent, sharp] It's GREY. Just this bit, the size of my hand.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It isn't dried out. It's just grey. Like somebody took the green out.
lines.script: [uneasy, quiet] It isn't dried out. It's just... grey. [thoughtful, slowly] Like somebody took the green out.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I'm keeping it. It's stuck.
lines.script: [determined] I'm keeping it. [short pause] [frustrated] It's STUCK.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Let me.
lines.script: [calm, confident] Let me.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: You're not trying.
lines.script: [accusing] You're not TRYING.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I'm trying, Rose. It's a marble and it's winning.
lines.script: [patient, dry] I'm trying, Rose. [deadpan] It's a marble... and it's winning.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: There's a little round hole in the side. Like somebody took a bite.
lines.script: [curious] There's a little round hole in the side. [amused] Like somebody took a BITE.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: And somebody left a burnt light bulb. Now they're littering at my pond too.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, annoyed] And somebody left a burnt light bulb. [warm Long Island accent, indignant] Now they're littering at MY pond too.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: The tin. Go, go, go.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, urgent, commanding] The tin. Go, go, GO.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Bye, marble. I'm coming back for you.
lines.script: [sweet] Bye, marble. [determined] I'm coming BACK for you.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That's a fish. That fish is bigger than the cab.
lines.script: [stunned, quiet] That's a fish. [awed, slowly] That fish is bigger than the CAB.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy was RIGHT?
lines.script: [disbelief] Boppy was RIGHT?

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Nobody tell him.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, whispers, urgent] Nobody tell him.

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: This morning I was a fish. Then there was a big flash. Now I am a BIG fish. With a hat.
lines.script: [bubbly, amazed] This morning I was a fish. [awed] Then there was a big flash. [proud] Now I am a BIG fish. [short pause] [delighted] With a hat.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tom, you stand in front of whoever it stares at. Cozy Rosie, make it laugh. Then we try again.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, firm, commanding] Tom, you stand in front of whoever it stares at. [warm Long Island accent, encouraging] Cozy Rosie, make it LAUGH. [warm Long Island accent, determined] Then we try again.

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: And this is for the small one. It's my shiniest thing.
lines.script: [shy, warm] And this is for the small one. [proud, softly] It's my SHINIEST thing.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It has a bug on it! I'm keeping it.
lines.script: [delighted, shrill] It has a BUG on it! [determined] I'm keeping it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: This one you can keep.
lines.script: [warm, amused] THIS one you can keep.

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: The old man with the cap. Is he coming tomorrow?
lines.script: [shy, hopeful] The old man with the cap. [quietly] Is he coming tomorrow?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy? He comes every day.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] Boppy? He comes EVERY day.

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: Good. Don't tell him I asked.
lines.script: [relieved, softly] Good. [whispers, sheepish] Don't tell him I asked.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy, the mud TALKED. And the mosquitoes. And a puddle.
lines.script: [excited, rushed] Boppy, the mud TALKED. And the mosquitoes. And a puddle.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The mud talked? Forty years in this town, the mud never said one word to me.
lines.script: [disbelief, playful] The mud talked? [complaining] Forty years in this town, the mud never said ONE word to me.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He gave me a present. Look.
lines.script: [proud, excited] He gave me a present. LOOK.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: That's real gold, Cozy Rosie. Gold like my teeth. Look.
lines.script: [impressed] That's real gold, Cozy Rosie. [proud, playful] Gold like my TEETH. Look.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Boppy has treasure in his mouth!
lines.script: [amazed, shouts] Boppy has TREASURE in his mouth!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: You put that somewhere safe. Gold is for keeping.
lines.script: [serious, warm] You put that somewhere safe. [quietly, firm] Gold is for keeping.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Next time something comes in that window, I'm coming. Stomach or no stomach.
lines.script: [determined] Next time something comes in that window, I'm coming. [wry] Stomach or NO stomach.
